findings.title: Facebook v26 transport remains unverified by its claimed contract source
findings.evidence: The harness asserts POST/form in expectContractCompliantTokenRequest and a bearer header for /me, but pinned OAuth2Client.php lines 264-271 constructs /oauth/access_token using GET, is copyrighted 2017, and contains no v26 binding. GRAPH_VERSION='v26.0' and the POST/bearer expectations are authored by the test. oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts replaces FacebookOAuthClient with a fake, so the current 323 unit/139 e2e passes cannot detect Graph v26 rejecting the implemented transport. This retests review-011 unchanged.
findings.expected_fix: Disable the unverified Facebook public flow or bind the real client to authoritative, version-specific transport evidence or sandbox verification.

implementation_guidance.approach: Because Facebook is deferred by the effective requirements, a valid safe outcome is to keep its public flow unreachable until an explicit requirement and supported contract exist. If retaining it, use a sandbox/test app or an official v26-compatible source that explicitly specifies the method, parameter channels, authentication channel, endpoints, and response fields, then exercise the real client against those semantics.
tests: Add a version-bound contract or sandbox test for the real FacebookOAuthClient authorization, token exchange, and /me request without replacing the client.
Retain negative assertions that client secret, authorization code, and access token never enter URLs or logs.
done_when: The public Facebook endpoint is disabled/unwired, or an authoritative source explicitly supports the configured version and exact implemented transport.
A test fails when method, parameter channel, authentication header, endpoint, or required response fields become incompatible.
Current-cycle validation and provenance are regenerated after the correction.

findings.title: Switching login/register views drops focus outside the modal
findings.evidence: The focused “Đăng ký” or “Đăng nhập” switch button is removed when AuthModal swaps views at lines 48-50. Dialog remains open, so useDismissableLayer's effect does not rerun or focus the replacement content. Its keydown handler only recovers activeIndex === -1 for Shift+Tab; forward Tab is not prevented and can move to focusable page content behind the portal. auth-modal.spec.tsx verifies the rendered view but never active focus or forward-Tab containment after either transition.
findings.expected_fix: Keep focus inside the dialog and move it predictably when switching between login and registration views.

implementation_guidance.approach: On each view transition, focus a stable target in the newly rendered view, such as its heading or first field, and/or harden useDismissableLayer so Tab from an active element outside the container is redirected inside. Preserve existing initial-focus and restoration behavior.
tests: After login-to-register and register-to-login transitions, assert document.activeElement is inside the dialog.
Press forward Tab and Shift+Tab after each transition and assert focus cannot reach background controls.
Retain Close/Escape/overlay dismissal and trigger-focus restoration tests; add a browser assertion at desktop and mobile viewports.
done_when: Both view transitions leave active focus within the dialog on a meaningful control.
Forward and reverse tabbing cannot escape to background content.
All existing dialog consumers and current responsive browser checks pass.

AC2: phone/password PUBLIC login, duplicate-submit prevention, and visible non-destructive errors
AC3: Google option only and safe Google OAuth success/cancel/error without a false session
AC4: switch login and registration inside the same modal
AC5: required registration fields, optional address, and field validation
AC6: exactly one atomic PUBLIC/LOCAL account graph and session; duplicate phone is safe
AC7: modal closes, auth state updates, and in-memory access/HttpOnly refresh policy is retained
AC8: anchored account popup and server/client logout behavior
AC9: design-system, accessibility, responsive, and route compatibility
AC10: reusable components and required behavior coverage

summary: Completed the full 66-file review and all seven passes. LOCAL/Google authentication, transactions, sessions, registration contracts, logout, responsive behavior, and provenance have strong current-cycle evidence. Two major issues remain: the Facebook flow relies on a contract harness that does not prove its v26 transport, and switching login/registration can move focus outside the dialog.
